title: Concerns About ‘WWII Allies’ at US-China Summit
gist: At the September 2026 US-China summit both leaders invoked their WWII alliance. Kawashima Shin argues this is unproblematic if it simply restates history (the US fought alongside the Republic of China against Japan) or signals a return to China's 2015-era 'New Model of Major-Country Relations' framing, implying concern arises only if the rhetoric serves other purposes.

themes.theme: WWII alliance rhetoric at the summit

insights.claim: At the September 2026 US-China summit, both leaders spoke of the United States and China having been WWII allies that fought together.
insights.so_what: Shared-history rhetoric at leader level signals an effort to warm US-China relations, relevant to tariff and tech-control risk.
insights.locator: At the U.S.-China summit in September 2026
insights.speaker: KAWASHIMA Shin

insights.claim: The US and China, in the form of the Republic of China, were indeed Allied nations fighting Japan in WWII, so remarks merely reaffirming that historical fact should raise no particular concern.
insights.so_what: The concern for Japan and Taiwan lies in what the rhetoric is used for, not in the historical fact itself.
insights.quote: if the summit remarks were intended simply to reaffirm that historical fact and invoke shared memory, then they should give rise to no particular concern
insights.locator: At the U.S.-China summit in September 2026
insights.speaker: KAWASHIMA Shin

themes.theme: 2015 precedent and 'New Model of Major-Country Relations'

insights.claim: In 2015, the 70th anniversary of the war's end, US-China relations were relatively stable and China emphasized fighting alongside the US and Western powers as a core Allied member that co-created the postwar order, while promoting a 'New Model of Major-Country Relations' with the US.
insights.so_what: China's WWII narrative tends to be deployed during periods it seeks stable great-power relations with Washington.
insights.locator: It is also worth recalling that in 2015
insights.speaker: KAWASHIMA Shin

insights.claim: If the summit's invocation of wartime partnership was meant to evoke 2015 and signal intent to restore the 'New Model of Major-Country Relations', that would be comprehensible as Chinese policy.
insights.so_what: A revived G2-style framing would imply Beijing seeking a bilateral great-power accommodation with Washington, which allies such as Japan watch warily.
insights.quote: signal an intention to restore the “New Model of Major-Country Relations,” that too would be comprehensible as a matter of Chinese policy
insights.locator: It is also worth recalling that in 2015
insights.speaker: KAWASHIMA Shin

insights.claim: The author implies that concern about the 'WWII allies' rhetoric is warranted only if it goes beyond historical reaffirmation or a return to 2015-style ties, since the wartime alliance was directed against Japan.
insights.so_what: US-China historical framing that casts Japan as the common enemy could strain US-Japan alliance optics.
insights.locator: At the U.S.-China summit in September 2026
insights.speaker: KAWASHIMA Shin
